terminology_notes.note: Specialty 227 was renamed from «Фізична терапія, ерготерапія» to «Терапія та реабілітація» (field 22 «Охорона здоров'я»); the new bachelor standard is MES order No. 1541 of 29.10.2024 and the master standard is MES order No. 1549 of 30.10.2024. Universities keep «Фізична терапія, ерготерапія» / «Фізична реабілітація» as programme (OPP) names under the renamed specialty.
terminology_notes.basis: https://www.dnu.dp.ua/docs/osvitni_programy/2022/b_227_TR_FTE_opp__2024.pdf — "227 «Терапія та реабілітація» ... наказом ... від 29.10.2024 р. №1541"; https://osvita.kpi.ua/sites/default/files/oop/i7_oppm_ft_2026.pdf — "Specialty 227 'Therapy and Rehabilitation,' ... Order ... No. 1549 dated October 30, 2024"

terminology_notes.note: Sub-specialisations appear as 227.01 «Фізична терапія» (new numbering) and 227.2 «Occupational Therapy» (older numbering). The bachelor educational qualification is «бакалавр терапії та реабілітації» with professional qualification «асистент фізичного терапевта» (physical therapist assistant) — i.e., the bachelor award is not itself 'physical therapist'.

terminology_notes.note: Completion document is called a 'state certificate' (TNMU) or 'certificate of completion' (KhNMU). What it confers differs by university: TNMU says it 'entitles to continue their studies for medico-biological direction at any university of Ukraine'; KhNMU says it 'gives the right to enroll in the 1st year for Ukrainian-language education without additional entrance examinations'; LNMU and ZSMPhU condition first-year enrolment on passing entrance exams. None of the snippets says the certificate guarantees admission.
terminology_notes.basis: https://junior.tdmu.edu.ua/english; https://knmu.edu.ua/en/navchalno-naukovyj-instytut-z-pidgotovky-inozemnyh-gromadyan-hnmu/pidgotovche-viddilennya/; https://universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/131/preparatory-department - 'After passing exams (Ukrainian Language, Biology, Chemistry and Physics)'; https://int.mphu.edu.ua/p_1276.html - 'enrolled in the University for first year of studying on the results of entrance examinations'.

terminology_notes.note: 'Medico-biological' / 'medical and biological' profile is the standard Ukrainian term for the pre-medical preparatory track (vs engineering/economic tracks). Core subjects: Ukrainian language, biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer science/informatics, country studies.
terminology_notes.basis: https://knmu.edu.ua/en/navchalno-naukovyj-instytut-z-pidgotovky-inozemnyh-gromadyan-hnmu/pidgotovche-viddilennya/ - 'Training profile - medical and biological'; https://junior.tdmu.edu.ua/english - 'Ukrainian (Russian) language, biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics and computer science'.

terminology_notes.note: 'Nostrification' = recognition of foreign education documents by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine; term used on portal university pages.
terminology_notes.basis: https://universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/60/documents/ (and sibling /documents/ pages) - 'foreign documents on education must be recognized (undergo nostrification procedure) in the Ministry of Education and Sciences of Ukraine during the first semester of study'.

terminology_notes.note: The 'Unified Interdepartmental Information System' (Єдина міжвідомча інформаційна система) is the official electronic applicant-account / invitation system referenced by universities; the studyinukraine.gov.ua portal is 'managed by the Ukrainian State Center for International Education'. terminology_notes.basis: https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/invitation-for-study/ and https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/?p=209 - 'The account is registered in the Unified Interdepartmental Informational System of Ukraine'; 'official Ukrainian Government website for international students, managed by the Ukrainian State Center for International Education'.

regulatory_notes.claim: Foreign applicants must first create a digital applicant account in the Unified Interdepartmental Informational System before applying to a Ukrainian university; up to 20 applications may be submitted; an application fee of 3100 UAH is paid once (undated portal pages; 3100 UAH also quoted as 'approximately 74 USD' on a university page - currency of date unknown).
regulatory_notes.basis: https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/invitation-for-study/ and https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/?p=209 - 'applicants must create a digital applicant account before applying to study at a university in Ukraine'; 'you can submit up to 20 applications'; 'the application fee is 3100 UAH and is paid once'. https://universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/87/how-to-get-invitation - 'The number of applications for an electronic invitation must not exceed 20'.

regulatory_notes.claim: The digital study invitation is an official electronic document signed online by the educational institution, valid for 6 months (one university page says 180 days), needed for the student visa and entry; its details are shared automatically with Ukrainian embassies and the State Border Guard Service. Universities state the Unified System is the exclusive/only route to an invitation.
regulatory_notes.basis: https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/invitation-for-study/ - 'official electronic document that is officially signed online by an authorized representative of the educational institution'; 'It is valid for 6 months'; 'automatically shared through the national system with Ukrainian embassies and the State Border Guard Service'. https://www.donnu.edu.ua/en/how-to-get-an-invitation-letter/ - 'the issuance of invitation letters for study and the admission process are carried out exclusively through the Unified Interdepartmental Information System'; https://knu.ua/pdfs/inter-stud/instructions-for-documents/How-to-obtain-invitation-letters-en.pdf - 'the only way to obtain a study invitation in Ukraine'; 'valid for 180 days from the date of its issuance'.

regulatory_notes.claim: Documents typically required for the invitation application: passport scan (often with notarised Ukrainian translation), previous education certificate/diploma plus transcript (legalisation/apostille where applicable), photo (one university: min 600x800 px, max 1 MB), proof of legal residence if different from nationality, signed personal-data consent form. Lists vary by university.
regulatory_notes.basis: https://universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/166/how-to-get-invitation ('Documents required for Invitation to study in Ukraine'); https://universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/87/how-to-get-invitation - 'notarised Ukrainian translation'; 'consent of the processing applicant's personal data'; https://universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/87/preparatory-department/ - 'citizens of the countries participating in the Hague Convention should stamp the Apostille on their documents'.

regulatory_notes.claim: Legal basis cited by universities for admitting foreigners: MES Order No. 1541 of 1 November 2013 (admission of foreigners and stateless persons), MES Order No. 504 of 5 May 2015 (recognition of foreign education documents), Cabinet Resolution No. 729 of 12 September 2018 (cited in VNMU 2025 rules). Foreign education documents must undergo recognition (nostrification) by the Ministry, usually during the first semester / before the second semester; the foreigner pays for it; failure can lead to expulsion.
